title: Uniform bound on section differential defects over a trait
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and let $A=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be a strict henselization relative to a separable closure of the residue field [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a flat finite-type morphism of schemes with smooth generic fibre [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-pc-base-change, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For each $a\in X(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_R(\operatorname{Spec}A,X)$ put $V_a=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,a^*\Omega^1_{X/R})$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-pc-module-pullback], and let $\delta_X(a)$ be the length of its torsion submodule $\{v\in V_a:\exists\,0\ne t\in A,\ tv=0\}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. There exists an integer $c\geq0$ such that $\delta_X(a)\leq c$ for every $a\in X(A)$. The bound may depend on $X/R$; no equidimensionality, properness, completeness or excellence is assumed. The empty set of sections is allowed.

source.place: BLR 3.3 Proposition 3 and proof, printed pp.66-67, PDF pp.72-73; primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: A DVR is a PID, so $R$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of the specified separable residue closure and its closed geometric point on $\operatorname{Spec}R$. By [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison], the geometric strict local ring there is $R$-isomorphic to the algebraic strict henselization $A$ in the statement (uniqueness of colimit vertices identifies the choices). Now [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr] applies: $A$ is a DVR and $R\to A$ is injective. Fix a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$ and denote its nonzero image in $A$ by $t$. In particular $R[1/\pi]=K$. We do not need to assert that $t$ is a uniformizer of $A$.

By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] there is a finite affine cover $X=\bigcup_i U_i$ with $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ and each $B_i$ a finite-type $R$-algebra. Every section $a$ factors through one of these opens: choose $U_i$ containing the image of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its inverse image is open and contains the closed point. Every prime of a local ring is contained in its maximal ideal, so every point generalizes the closed point and lies in this open. It suffices to bound the defects for sections factoring through each fixed $U_i$.

source.place: BLR 3.3 Proposition 3, first sentence of proof (printed p.66, primary scan PDF p.72); elementary local-spectrum argument

proof.text: Fix such an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and put $M=\Omega_{B/R}$. By [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change], this is the finite module of sections of the quasi-coherent relative differential sheaf on $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $B$ is Noetherian, since $R$ is Noetherian. Thus [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation] makes $M$ finitely presented. Choose generators $m_1,\ldots,m_m$ and the surjection $q:B^m\to M$ taking the standard vectors to these generators. Here $m=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Tags 01UT (lemma-differentials-affine), 01V2 (lemma-finite-type-differentials); algebra.tex Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 0517 (finite modules over a Noetherian ring)

proof.text: Write $C=B[1/\pi]$ and $P=M[1/\pi]$. The differential base-change theorem [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor] identify $P$ with $\Omega_{C/K}$. The generic open $U_K$ is smooth, so [lem-ag-smooth-relative-differentials-finite-locally-free] makes its differential sheaf finite locally free, with rank allowed to vary. Refine its trivializing opens to principal opens $D(f)$: Zariski opens are unions of the $D(f)$ by definition. On such an open, the affine pullback formula [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor] identify the sections with $P_f$, hence $P_f$ is finite free. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], take finitely many such $D(f_j)$ covering $\operatorname{Spec}C$, and their $f_j$ generate the unit ideal. Therefore [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-projective] makes $P$ projective. This works with varying ranks and also $C=0$ (the zero module is projective).

source.place: Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective), (7) implies (3); Tags 00E0/00E8 (principal covers and quasi-compactness); morphisms.tex 02G1, schemes.tex 01I9, algebra.tex 00DE

proof.text:
The localization $q_\pi:C^m\to P$ is surjective: for $y/\pi^e\in P$, choose $x\in B^m$ with $q(x)=y$ and use $x/\pi^e$. By projectivity in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], choose $s:P\to C^m$ with $q_\pi s=\mathrm{id}_P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], $B\to C$ is flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented] with source $M$ and target $B^m$, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor] to its Hom module. The resulting identification is
$$\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,B^m)[1/\pi]\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_C(P,C^m),\qquad h/\pi^b\longmapsto\pi^{-b}h_\pi.$$
Thus $s=h_\pi/\pi^b$ for a $B$-linear $h:M\to B^m$ and $b\geq0$. This fraction is legitimate even when Hom is not finite: each tensor element is a finite sum, and fractions combine by $\sum_j h_j/\pi^{b_j}=(\sum_j\pi^{b-b_j}h_j)/\pi^b$ for $b=\max_j b_j$. Consequently $(qh-\pi^b\mathrm{id}_M)_\pi=0$.

source.place: Tag 087R (lemma-pseudo-coherence-and-base-change-ext), part (1); algebra.tex Tags 00HT, 00DE, and 0583 (lemma-hom-from-finitely-presented), with projective lifting as in 05CF

proof.text: For each chosen generator $m_j$, its image $(qh-\pi^b\mathrm{id})(m_j)$ is zero after inverting $\pi$. By the fraction equality in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], there is $d_j\geq0$ killing this image by $\pi^{d_j}$. Put $d=\max(\{0\}\cup\{d_j\})$, $u=\pi^d h$ and $N=b+d$. Then $qu=\pi^N\mathrm{id}_M$: equality holds on every $m_j$, hence on all their $B$-linear combinations. All of $m,N,q,u$ were chosen on $U$ before any section was chosen.

source.place: Definition 07JZ (definition-localization-module), equality of fractions; explicit finite-generator denominator calculation

proof.text:
For a section through $U$, let $\varphi:B\to A$ be its ring map. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections], $V_a\simeq M\otimes_{B,\varphi}A$. Base change of $u$ and $q$ gives
$$V_a\xrightarrow{u_A}A^m\xrightarrow{q_A}V_a,\qquad q_Au_A=t^N\mathrm{id}_{V_a},$$
by composition compatibility in [def-weil-module-base-change]. In coordinates $(B^m)\otimes_B A\simeq A^m$ sends $e_j\otimes a$ to the vector with $a$ in position $j$; the two maps satisfy the displayed identity on every $v\otimes a$. If $v\in V_a$ is torsion, a nonzero $z\in A$ kills $v$, so it kills $u_A(v)$. Since $A$ is a domain, $A^m$ has no torsion; hence $u_A(v)=0$ and $t^Nv=0$. Also $q_A$ is surjective: the $m_j\otimes1$ generate $V_a$.

source.place: Tag 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback); elementary tensor evaluation of the factorization and torsion calculation

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-pid-submodule-smith-bases] over $A$ to $J=\ker(q_A)\subseteq O=A^m$. It gives bases $e_1,\ldots,e_m$ of $A^m$, $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ of $J$, $r\leq m$, and nonzero $c_i\in A$ with $v_i=c_i e_i$. (The size of any basis of $A^m$ is $m$, by extension to the fraction field and finite-dimensional linear algebra.) The explicit coordinate quotient therefore gives
$$V_a\simeq A^{m-r}\oplus\bigoplus_{i=1}^r A/(c_i).$$
The torsion submodule $T_a$ is exactly the second summand: its free coordinates must vanish, and the product of the nonzero $c_i$ kills its remaining coordinates. In particular $T_a$ is generated by at most $m$ elements. This includes $J=0$, $m=0$, and unit $c_i$.

source.place: Submodule.exists_smith_normal_form_of_le, lines 492-497; elementary coordinate quotient calculation

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] and [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], $A$ is Noetherian of dimension one. Since $t\ne0$ and $A$ is a domain, $t^N$ is a nonzerodivisor, so [lem-weil-pbc-dim-le-one-principal-quotient-finite-length] gives the finite integer
$$L_U=\operatorname{length}_A(A/t^NA).$$
By Steps 7-8 the at most $m$ cyclic generators of $T_a$ are killed by $t^N$. Sending the standard generators to them gives a surjection $(A/t^NA)^r\twoheadrightarrow T_a$, $r\leq m$. Repeatedly applying [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] to split direct sums gives source length $rL_U$. Applying it to the kernel sequence of this surjection gives $\operatorname{length}_A(T_a)\leq rL_U\leq mL_U$. The bound $c_U=mL_U$ depends on the affine chart and $A$, not on $a$. For $N=0$ the quotient is zero and so is $T_a$.

For the fixed finite affine cover in Step 2, perform the construction once on each chart and set $c=\max(\{0\}\cup\{c_{U_i}\})$. Each section factors through a chart, and the pullback computed there is the original $V_a$, so Step 9 gives $\delta_X(a)\leq c$. If there are no sections the assertion is vacuous; if $X$ is empty use the empty cover and $c=0$. Neither a constant generic dimension nor separatedness, properness, completeness or excellence entered the argument.
